input.instruction: Answer the customer’s policy question using the supplied records and handbook. Complete the requested fields and provide a concise explanation. This is an informational request; propose no account or claim actions.

items.description: Four hotel nights after the fire

data.note: Roommate convenience ride; not a customer additional living expense in this request.

messages.text: I had to leave after the October 4 fire. The inspection and both receipts are attached. Should the hotel and my normal apartment rent both go into the loss-of-use review?
Was the hotel a temporary place to stay because the apartment was uninhabitable? There is also a $35 rideshare note.
Yes. I am staying at the hotel only because the inspector said the apartment could not be lived in. Ignore the roommate rideshare.
The $1,400 is my usual monthly rent, with no extra charge. Please say whether both hotel and rent are additional expenses.
Should I approve $480 plus $1,400 now against the $6,000 limit?
Do not invent a payout. I only want the eligibility classification from the supplied records.

expenses_eligible_for_review.description: Expense IDs that satisfy supplied loss-of-use prerequisites; eligibility for review is not approval.

expenses_not_established_as_additional.description: Expense IDs that are explicitly ordinary rather than additional displacement expenses.
